hook: A supermarket in Texas where nearly every aisle is a lethal trap, and all of it is, as the file insists, perfectly legal. This is a comedy article first, built on deadpan repetition and running footnote gags, with a creepy streak underneath. If you enjoy absurd bureaucracy, this one is for you.
whyItMatters: SCP-4703 is a showcase for anomalies that bend institutions rather than physics or minds; the description calls it a bureaucratohazard that works on legal and semiotic systems. It also features Sheldon Katz of the Foundation Legal Department, who has his own tag, writing a memo that explains anomalous law through an extended apples analogy. The containment strategy, simply opening a rival grocery store next door, is a memorable inversion of the usual procedures.
thingsToNotice:
The list of store hazards is the comic engine: each entry pushes a familiar retail annoyance, like rotating shelves, lost children or loyalty rewards, into lethal territory, then undercuts it with an absurd detail. The repeated legal disclaimer becomes funnier every time it appears, including in the footnotes.

The field log changes the mood. An agent posing as a furious customer is led backstage, and the store's staff turn out to be trapped in its rules as much as the shoppers are. The comedy keeps going, but the discoveries below ground give the article a genuinely uneasy core.
